title: Bridging the knowledge gaps: A global mapping of capacity building offerings on climate change and health
content:
by Jaafar Tfayli, Sara Kassab, Zahraa Chamseddine, Shadi Saleh, Nour El Arnaout

Climate change is an escalating global health threat with disproportionate effects in climate-vulnerable regions. Building capacity at the intersection of climate and health is essential to equip healthcare systems and professionals to assess risks and sustain resilient services. This study maps online publicly accessible capacity-building offerings on climate change and health, focusing on accessibility and applicability to the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. A rapid web mapping review identified courses, non-accredited certificates, accredited certificates, and diplomas offered by universities and institutions, excluding master's and PhD programs. Learning outcomes/objectives and metadata (provider type, geography, modality, language, credentialing) were extracted and thematically coded to characterize targeted domains. Twenty-two offerings were identified. Most were courses 82% (n = 18), followed by non-accredited certificates 9% (n = 2), accredited certificates 4.5% (n = 1), and diplomas 4.5% (n = 1). Providers included academic institutions 50% (n = 11), international organizations 27% (n = 6), and e-learning platforms 23% (n = 5). Delivery was predominantly online, 77% (n = 17), with some hybrid, 23% (n = 5) (Fig 2A). Nearly all offerings were in English, 96% (n = 21), with one multilingual; none were in Arabic. Provider geography was largely global (n = 13) or based in the United States (n = 6), with isolated entries from Germany (n = 1), Australia (n = 1), and Kenya (n = 1). No offerings originated from the MENA region. Thematically, programs emphasized climate Change and health policy, governance, leadership, and health impacts, while equity, resilience, competency alignment, applied operations, and stackable credentialing were minimally addressed. Overall, the landscape remains fragmented and rooted in the global north. Key gaps include co-designed, practice-oriented training with climate-vulnerable regions, especially MENA, embedding clear competencies, authentic assessment, and multilingual accessibility.
